s: Quebec's oldest municipal library, lending since 1899
w: Tucked into the northwest corner of Westmount Park at 4574 Sherbrooke Street West, this Robert Findlay-designed building has been lending books since 1899, one of the oldest library buildings standing in Canada, and the oldest municipal library anywhere in Quebec.
_facts: Located at 4574 Sherbrooke Street West, Westmount, Quebec, in the northwest corner of Westmount Park
Designed by Robert Findlay, opened in 1899
One of the oldest library buildings in Canada, and the oldest municipal library in Quebec

w: Montreal's flagship English-language theatre company has worked out of this building since 1969, first as a tenant, then as owner after a 1974 renovation by architect Victor Prus. Two very different rooms resulted: the roughly 220-seat black box C1, and the 420-seat proscenium stage of C2.
_facts: Founded 1969 by Maurice Podbrey with The Centaur Foundation for the Performing Arts
The city's flagship English-language theatre company
Leased the partially renovated auditorium 1969-1973, purchased the building in 1974, $1.3 million renovation by architect Victor Prus, reopened 1975
Original black box theatre renamed C1, seats approximately 220; newer venue C2 seats approximately 420
